newsitem.title: UK: NWE fuel oil barges steady, cargo offers unchanged.
newsitem.headline: NWE fuel oil barges steady, cargo offers unchanged.

text.p: European high sulphur fuel oil barges ended largely steady on Thursday in a quiet market, low sulphur barges traded a little weaker while high sulphur cargoes were offered at steady prices in a quiet market, traders said.
Afternoon activity in high sulphur fuel oil barges was thin, with deals at $85 and $85.50 fob ARA after earlier trades at $85 and $86.
An early morning trade was done at $83 per tonne fob Rotterdam but traders dismissed it as a failed attempt to push prices down.
"$85/$86 is the buy/sell range; $83 is not the market. Someone was trying to push levels down," one trader said.

Another said traded volume for the day was about 11,000 tonnes. A second trader agreed, saying: "On average demand is on the low side". Low sulphur fuel oil barges traded at slightly lower levels than last done.
A French refiner in the ARA area said it sold two 15,000 tonne low sulphur barges to two Belgian firms at $94.50 fob Flushing, about $1 lower than recent deals.
"Today is the first time we did any deals in a few days," the seller said.
Offers were in the $95/$95.50 region while bids were at $94.
"The last asking level $96 is difficult to achieve at the moment. There's not a lot of demand," the seller said.
No trades were heard in high sulphur cargoes, but one seller with bunker grade material at $82 fob said he would consider bids at $1 lower, a level still deemed too high by some traders.
Another cargo was still being offered by a trader at $79 fob.
Traders said a cargo of Russian E-4 was heard bought on Wednesday by a British major at three means plus a $2.50 premium -- a price said to be a reflection of current market value.
One percent was being offered at higher numbers in the mid-nineties but buyers were still far below.
"Some refiners are trying to get high numbers but this is unrealistic. I heard offers in the $96 range, but buyers are in the low nineties," one trader said.
